s1.syndrome_frame: Acute worsening of a chronic facial rash with pustular lesions
salient_findings: Confluent erythematous, edematous plaques in the bilateral periorbital areas
Numerous 2- to 3-mm pustules, some coalescing into lakes of pus
Pustules also noted in the perioral area
key_facts: 14-year-old girl presented with a worsening facial rash
Rash began 6 days earlier as red papules over the left cheek
Rash progressed markedly over the next 3 days
Patient had a history of atopic dermatitis diagnosed 2 years prior
Patient had been applying triamcinolone 0.1% ointment twice daily for 2 years
Patient stopped the ointment completely 3 days before presentation
Patient denied fever, systemic symptoms, or personal or family history of atopy
Patient was afebrile and appeared well on examination

shortlist.why_kept: Patient had been applying triamcinolone 0.1% ointment for 2 years and stopped 3 days before presentation, which could have triggered the acute worsening of the rash

shortlist.label: Perioral dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with a worsening facial rash, particularly in the periorbital areas, which is consistent with perioral dermatitis

shortlist.label: Acne fulminans
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's rash progressed markedly over 3 days, and the presence of pustules and confluent erythematous plaques could be indicative of acne fulminans

shortlist.label: Demodex folliculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of atopic dermatitis and the presence of pustules could be related to Demodex folliculitis

shortlist.label: Papulopustular rosacea
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms, including the presence of pustules and erythematous plaques, are consistent with papulopustular rosacea
